answer: A chip's power-draw curve under a standard workload is a fingerprint of its silicon and board. The agent runs the workload and submits the signed power profile. A willow bends but never breaks the same way twice — each chip's curve is unique. A fable of identical curves fails, because manufacturing variation guarantees differences. A falcon-eyed check compares new profiles against the registry, and identical curves from supposedly different devices are rejected as clones.
